verdict.rationale: EDD's own e-Services documentation shows that employers can authorize a power of attorney and that third-party representatives (tax preparers, bookkeepers, agents, accountants) can enroll to manage a client's payroll tax account. That establishes a delegated-access mechanism, but the pack never says what that access permits or prohibits. Missing for 10: named authorization forms, a published breakdown of third-party roles and permission scopes, any statement of which signatures or declarations must stay personal to the employer, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: You are a third-party representative, such as a tax preparer, bookkeeper, agent, or accountant, enrolling to manage your client's employer payroll tax account.
